answers.sql:
WITH cm_5_cte AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(opex) AS opex
    , SUM(opex_budget_to_date) AS opex_budget_to_date
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('quarter', pnl_src_10000.period) AS metric_time__quarter
      , accounts_src_10000.account_type AS account__account_type
      , pnl_src_10000.actual_gbp AS opex
      , pnl_src_10000.budget_gbp_closed AS opex_budget_to_date
    FROM "finance-tickmark"."main"."fct_pnl" pnl_src_10000
    LEFT OUTER JOIN
      "finance-tickmark"."main"."dim_account" accounts_src_10000
    ON
      pnl_src_10000.account_code = accounts_src_10000.account_code
  ) subq_5
  WHERE (
    account__account_type = 'opex'
  ) AND (
    metric_time__quarter = '2026-07-01'
  )
)

SELECT
  MAX(cm_5_cte.opex) AS opex
  , MAX(cm_5_cte.opex_budget_to_date) AS opex_budget_to_date
  , MAX(subq_11.opex_variance) AS opex_variance
FROM cm_5_cte
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT
    opex - opex_budget_to_date AS opex_variance
  FROM (
    SELECT
      opex
      , opex_budget_to_date
    FROM cm_5_cte
  ) subq_10
) subq_11

answers.sql:
WITH sma_10001_cte AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', period) AS metric_time__quarter
    , account_code AS account
    , entity_code AS legal_entity
    , actual_gbp AS __revenue
    , budget_gbp_closed AS __revenue_budget_to_date
    , actual_gbp_cc AS __revenue_constant_currency
  FROM "finance-tickmark"."main"."fct_pnl" pnl_src_10000
)

, rss_10001_cte AS (
  SELECT
    account_type
    , account_code AS account
  FROM "finance-tickmark"."main"."dim_account" accounts_src_10000
)

, rss_10003_cte AS (
  SELECT
    entity_code
    , entity_code AS legal_entity
  FROM "finance-tickmark"."main"."dim_legal_entity" legal_entities_src_10000
)

SELECT
  MAX(subq_11.revenue_constant_currency) AS revenue_constant_currency
  , MAX(subq_11.revenue_budget_to_date) AS revenue_budget_to_date
  , MAX(subq_23.fx_impact_on_revenue) AS fx_impact_on_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    SUM(revenue_constant_currency) AS revenue_constant_currency
    , SUM(revenue_budget_to_date) AS revenue_budget_to_date
  FROM (
    SELECT
      sma_10001_cte.metric_time__quarter AS metric_time__quarter
      , rss_10001_cte.account_type AS account__account_type
      , rss_10003_cte.entity_code AS legal_entity__entity_code
      , sma_10001_cte.__revenue_budget_to_date AS revenue_budget_to_date
      , sma_10001_cte.__revenue_constant_currency AS revenue_constant_currency
    FROM sma_10001_cte
    LEFT OUTER JOIN
      rss_10001_cte
    ON
      sma_10001_cte.account = rss_10001_cte.account
    LEFT OUTER JOIN
      rss_10003_cte
    ON
      sma_10001_cte.legal_entity = rss_10003_cte.legal_entity
  ) subq_7
  WHERE (
    account__account_type = 'revenue'
  ) AND (
    legal_entity__entity_code = 'US01'
  ) AND (
    metric_time__quarter = '2026-07-01'
  )
) subq_11
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT
    revenue - revenue_constant_currency AS fx_impact_on_revenue
  FROM (
    SELECT
      SUM(revenue) AS revenue
      , SUM(revenue_constant_currency) AS revenue_constant_currency
    FROM (
      SELECT
        sma_10001_cte.metric_time__quarter AS metric_time__quarter
        , rss_10001_cte.account_type AS account__account_type
        , rss_10003_cte.entity_code AS legal_entity__entity_code
        , sma_10001_cte.__revenue AS revenue
        , sma_10001_cte.__revenue_constant_currency AS revenue_constant_currency
      FROM sma_10001_cte
      LEFT OUTER JOIN
        rss_10001_cte
      ON
        sma_10001_cte.account = rss_10001_cte.account
      LEFT OUTER JOIN
        rss_10003_cte
      ON
        sma_10001_cte.legal_entity = rss_10003_cte.legal_entity
    ) subq_18
    WHERE (
      account__account_type = 'revenue'
    ) AND (
      legal_entity__entity_code = 'US01'
    ) AND (
      metric_time__quarter = '2026-07-01'
    )
  ) subq_22
) subq_23

A positive opex variance is bad, because it is adverse. Under the FP&A sign convention a variance is always actual minus budget, and for costs (COGS and opex) a positive variance is adverse. The opex variance definition says the same: positive means overspend, measured on closed months only.

citations.quote: Revenue and costs are both stored as positive amounts. A variance is always **actual minus budget**. For revenue, a positive variance is favourable. For costs (COGS and opex), a positive variance is adverse.

Actual minus budget for closed months. Positive is adverse (overspend).
Definition: Actual minus budget, closed months only. FP&A policy sign convention.
Owner: Group FP&A

answers.question: Is a positive opex variance good or bad?
answers.explanation: A positive opex variance is bad, because it is adverse. Under the FP&A sign convention a variance is always actual minus budget, and for costs (COGS and opex) a positive variance is adverse. The opex variance definition says the same: positive means overspend, measured on closed months only.
